title: GitHub - Ri4dH/failtrace: Stop guessing why CI failed. Reproduce it locally.
excerpt: Stop guessing why CI failed. Reproduce it locally. - Ri4dH/failtrace
content_html:
Stop guessing why CI failed. Reproduce it locally.

Paste a failed GitHub Actions run URL. FailTrace finds the job and step that failed, matches them to the workflow file at that exact commit, pulls the failure out of the logs, and tells you what stands between you and reproducing it on your machine.

failtrace inspect https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789   # why did it fail?
failtrace plan    https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789   # how would it be reproduced?
failtrace repro   https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789   # reproduce it in Docker

Status: early development. All three commands work. repro covers Linux jobs whose failing step is a run: script. See the roadmap and limitations.

Why not act?

act runs your workflows locally, and it's great at that. FailTrace answers a different question: why did this particular run fail, and can I make it fail the same way here?

  • It starts from a failed run, not a workflow file. You get the exact commit, attempt, job, matrix combination, and failing step. Nothing to configure.
  • It focuses on the failure. The goal is to replay only what the failing step needs, not the whole workflow.
  • It gives you a verdict. You get a diagnosis now. Later you'll also get reproduced / not reproduced / flaky, plus what differed between CI and your machine.

Example

Real output for a failed prometheus/prometheus run (trimmed):

✗ CI · prometheus/prometheus
  "remote/otlp: remove delta-to-cumulative conversion"
  pull_request · on codex/remove-otlp-deltatocumulative · @ cf7d324 · attempt 1 · failure

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
✗ Job: Go tests  (failure)
  Runner     ubuntu-latest → ubuntu-26.04 (20261116.202.1) · runner 2.338.2
  Workflow   .github/workflows/ci.yml → jobs.test_go

  Steps
    ✓  5  Run make GO_ONLY=1 SKIP_GOLANGCI_LINT=1
    ✓  6  Run go test ./tsdb/ -test.tsdb-isolation=false
    ✗  7  Run make -C documentation/examples/remote_storage  ← failed here
    ○  8  Run make -C documentation/examples (skipped)

  Failed step  #7 Run make -C documentation/examples/remote_storage
    shell: sh -e {0}
    $ make -C documentation/examples/remote_storage

  Diagnosis  files out of date (a check produced a git diff) · exit code 2

  Log excerpt (10 lines around the first error in "Run make -C documentation/examples/remote_storage")
    │ >> running check for unused/missing packages in go.mod
    │ go mod tidy
    │ go: downloading github.com/oapi-codegen/nullable v1.1.0
    │ diff --git a/documentation/examples/remote_storage/go.mod b/documentation/examples/remote_storage/go.mod
    │ --- a/documentation/examples/remote_storage/go.mod
    │ +++ b/documentation/examples/remote_storage/go.mod

  Reproduction notes
    ! job runs inside container quay.io/prometheus/golang-builder:1.27-base

The log ends with hundreds of lines of go.sum diff. FailTrace centres the excerpt on the first error line so you see the cause, go mod tidy changing go.mod, instead of the noise after it.

Install

macOS and Linux, using the install script. It downloads the latest release for your platform and verifies its SHA-256 checksum:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ri4dH/failtrace/main/scripts/install.sh | sh

It installs to /usr/local/bin if that's writable, otherwise to ~/.local/bin. Set FAILTRACE_INSTALL_DIR to choose, or FAILTRACE_VERSION=v0.1.0 to pin a release.

Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows (amd64 and arm64) are on the releases page, with a checksums.txt.

With Go 1.24+:

go install github.com/Ri4dH/failtrace/cmd/failtrace@latest

From source:

git clone https://github.com/Ri4dH/failtrace
cd failtrace
go build -o bin/failtrace ./cmd/failtrace

Usage

# All failed jobs in the latest attempt of a run
failtrace inspect https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789

# A single job (the URL you get from clicking a job in the Actions UI)
failtrace inspect https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789/job/987654321

# A specific attempt of a re-run workflow
failtrace inspect https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789/attempts/2

# Show more log context, or emit JSON for scripts and other tools
failtrace inspect -n 60 <run-url>
failtrace inspect --json <run-url> | jq '.failed_jobs[0].failure'

# A compact summary to paste into a coding assistant
failtrace inspect --llm <run-url> | pbcopy
Flag Default Description
--json off Print the report as JSON
--llm off Print a compact plain-text summary for a language model's prompt
-n, --lines 25 Log lines to show from the failed step
--job all failed Inspect only this job ID

Colour output turns off automatically when stdout is not a terminal, or when NO_COLOR is set.

For coding assistants: --llm

--llm prints only what a model needs to fix the failure: the failing step, its command and relevant env, the exit code, errors, failing tests, and the log from the first error. It leaves out step lists, runner metadata, the variables setup actions export, and go test -v progress lines and progress bars. Error lines appear once, and matrix jobs that failed the same way collapse into one line.

Measured on real failed runs, compared with the raw logs of their failed jobs:

Run Raw logs --llm
stretchr/testify (go vet + Go version) 38 KB 1.2 KB
pytest-dev/pytest (pytest failure) 125 KB 3.7 KB
vitejs/vite (two Vitest failures) 306 KB 3.9 KB
prometheus/prometheus (Go test failure) 8.3 MB 1.8 KB

Authentication

FailTrace needs a GitHub token, even for public repositories, because the logs API requires one. It looks in this order:

  1. GITHUB_TOKEN
  2. GH_TOKEN
  3. gh auth token (if you use the GitHub CLI, this already works)

Private repositories need a token that can read Actions on that repo. GitHub Enterprise Server URLs work too: the API base becomes https://<host>/api/v3.

What inspect reports

  • Run context: workflow, event, branch, commit, attempt.

  • Job → workflow mapping: finds the job definition, including jobs named like test (ubuntu-latest, 1.22) or Lint ${{ matrix.tool }}, and recovers the matrix values.

  • Runner: the requested label and the actual runner image and version, from the log.

  • Failed step: its definition (run, uses, with, env, shell, working directory). The command shown is the one printed in the log, with expressions already filled in.

  • Diagnosis: exit code, error annotations, failing test names (Go, pytest, Jest, Vitest, Cargo, RSpec), and a category:

    Category Example signal
    test --- FAIL: TestX, FAILED tests/x.py::test_y
    build error TS2304, undefined: foo, error[E0425]
    dependency npm ERR! code ERESOLVE, missing go.sum entry
    lint golangci-lint, eslint, ruff steps
    generated-diff a check that printed diff --git (tidy, codegen, formatters)
    timeout exceeded the maximum execution time
    out-of-memory exit code 137, heap out of memory

  • Reproduction notes: anything that makes a local repro harder. That means service containers, job containers, secrets the step uses, reusable workflows, and macOS or Windows runners.

It also explains edge cases instead of failing silently: runs that failed before any job started, dynamic workflows with no file in the repo, and logs that have expired.

Planning a reproduction

failtrace plan works out how to reproduce the failed job locally and prints the plan. It doesn't run anything yet.

failtrace plan https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789
failtrace plan --job 987654321 <run-url>     # pick a job when several failed
failtrace plan --json <run-url>              # the full plan, including every env var

Real output for a failed pytest-dev/pytest job (trimmed):

Reproduction plan · pytest-dev/pytest
  Job        build (ubuntu-py311)  (jobs.build)
  Verdict    PARTIAL: can run, but the warnings below may make it differ from CI
  Image      ubuntu:26.04  linux/amd64
             matches the runner image ubuntu-26.04 20261111.196.1
  Commit     c484767

  Toolchains
    python   3.11.18    exact · asked for "3.11" · from actions/setup-python@6d4fd22
    uv       0.13.8     exact · from astral-sh/setup-uv@11f9893

  Steps
    1  checkout    Run actions/checkout@3d3c42e
                    pytest-dev/pytest @ c484767 (merge of 58b8dae into 50234b4)
    2  skip        Download Package
                    — downloads artifacts from another job
    3  toolchain   Set up Python 3.11
                    → install python 3.11.18
    4  composite   Run pytest-dev/pytest/.github/actions/setup-tox@c484767
                    — composite action; its steps follow
    5    toolchain   Run astral-sh/setup-uv@11f9893
                      → install uv 0.13.8
    6    run         $ if [ -n "$PYTHON_VERSION" ]; then  (+4 lines)
    7  run         Test with coverage  ← failed in CI
                    $ tox run -e py311-coverage --installpkg `find dist/*.tar.gz`
                    shell: /usr/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail {0}

  Issues
    ! [step 2] actions/download-artifact@9000827 downloads artifacts produced by another job or run; files it provides will be missing locally
    i [step 1] CI tested the merge of PR head 58b8dae into base 50234b4 (merge commit c484767), not the PR branch alone; the plan checks out that merge commit

How the plan is built:

  • The log is the source of truth for what ran. Scripts, shells and environment come from the step headers GitHub prints, so ${{ matrix.* }} and other expressions are already filled in. Composite actions show their inner steps.
  • The exact commit CI tested. For pull requests that's a merge commit GitHub created, not your branch head. This is a common reason a failure "doesn't happen locally".
  • The exact toolchain versions. "3.11" in the workflow becomes 3.11.18, read from the runner's tool cache paths. When the log doesn't show a version, it reads version files such as go.mod (including toolchain), .nvmrc, .python-version, .tool-versions and packageManager in package.json.
  • The right base image. A job container: is used as is. Otherwise it picks the Ubuntu version matching the runner image the job actually got.
  • What to skip and what to flag. Caches, uploads and coverage reporters are skipped. Downloaded artifacts, service containers, secrets, unknown actions, and tools used without a setup step (they were preinstalled on the runner) are reported as issues.

The verdict is ready (nothing known to be missing), partial (it can run, but some parts are approximated or missing) or blocked (the failing step is an action, not a script, so it can't be replayed yet).

Supported setup actions: actions/setup-go, setup-node, setup-python, setup-java, setup-dotnet, ruby/setup-ruby, dtolnay/rust-toolchain, actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain, pnpm/action-setup, pnpm/setup, astral-sh/setup-uv, oven-sh/setup-bun and denoland/setup-deno.

Reproducing a failure

failtrace repro builds the plan and runs it in Docker, then compares the result with CI's failure.

failtrace repro <run-url>
failtrace repro --keep <run-url>                     # keep the container to poke around afterwards
API_TOKEN=... failtrace repro --secret API_TOKEN <run-url>
failtrace repro --toolchain node=20.11.1 <run-url>   # fill in or override a toolchain
failtrace repro --platform linux/arm64 <run-url>     # run natively on Apple silicon (faster, less exact)
failtrace repro --runs 10 <run-url>                  # is it flaky?
failtrace repro --shell <run-url>                    # debug inside the container afterwards
failtrace repro --report repro.md <run-url>          # Markdown report for an issue or PR

You need Docker (Docker Desktop, colima, OrbStack, …) and git.

Real output for a failed stretchr/testify run, where go vet failed under Go oldstable. FailTrace resolved oldstable to the exact Go 1.26.9 build CI used, checked out the PR merge commit CI tested, and replayed the steps:

$ failtrace repro --platform linux/arm64 https://github.com/stretchr/testify/actions/runs/39247781971
Reproducing stretchr/testify · build (oldstable) · plan ready
▶ Image       failtrace-env:08414601e6c4aef4 (cached)
▶ Workspace   stretchr/testify @ 9272105
▶ [3/5]       Run ./.ci.gogenerate.sh
  ✓ exit code 0 (17.7s)
▶ [4/5]       Run ./.ci.gofmt.sh
  ✓ exit code 0 (7.4s)
▶ [5/5]       Run ./.ci.govet.sh  ← failed in CI
    │ assert/assertion_compare_test.go:85:13: non-constant format string in call to (*testing.common).Errorf
    │ assert/assertion_compare_test.go:94:13: non-constant format string in call to (*testing.common).Errorf
  ✗ exit code 1 (10.7s)

✓ Reproduced: the step fails locally the same way it failed in CI
  • the same error: assert/assertion_compare_test.go:<n>:<n>: non-constant format string in call to (*testing.common).Errorf

                 CI                           Local
  Exit code      1                            1
  Failure        lint / format check          lint / format check

  Steps      4 passed · 1 failed (39s total)
  Image      failtrace-env:08414601e6c4aef4 linux/arm64

  Differences from CI
    - the image is plain ubuntu:24.04 with common runner packages; GitHub's runner image has far more preinstalled
    - steps run as root; on GitHub's runners they run as the `runner` user with passwordless sudo
    - running linux/arm64, but CI ran linux/amd64

Without --platform, the job runs as linux/amd64 like CI did. On an Apple silicon Mac that means emulation: the same reproduction took about 9 minutes instead of 40 seconds, with the same verdict.

What happens:

  1. Environment image. The plan's base image, plus the packages every GitHub Ubuntu runner has (git, curl, build tools, python3, jq, sudo, …), plus the toolchains. Go, Node and Python are the same builds setup-go, setup-node and setup-python download, installed under /opt/hostedtoolcache where CI keeps them. uv, pnpm and Rust are installed from their releases. The image is tagged by a hash of its contents, so it's only built once per environment.

  2. Workspace. The exact commit CI tested is fetched on your machine the way actions/checkout does it, with the same fetch depth, and mounted at the same path as on the runner (/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>, or /__w/... for container jobs). If GitHub has since replaced a pull request's merge commit, the merge is recreated locally.

  3. Services. Service containers start in the job container's network namespace, so localhost:5432 and postgres:5432 both work, and FailTrace waits for their health checks.

  4. Steps. Run steps replay in order with the shell, environment and working directory CI used. $GITHUB_ENV and $GITHUB_PATH carry over between steps. The failing step's output streams live.

  5. Verdict.

    • reproduced: the same tests failed, or the same error or exit code.
    • different-failure
    • not-reproduced: the step passed locally.
    • diverged: an earlier step failed locally, so the failing step never ran.
    • flaky: with --runs, the step failed in some runs but not all.

    A list of known differences from CI comes with every verdict.

Flaky failures: --runs N

The setup steps run once, then the failing step runs N times in the same container, so repeats are cheap. If it fails only some of the time, the verdict is flaky ("the step failed in 3 of 10 runs"). Go's test cache is bypassed for these runs (GOFLAGS=-count=1). Otherwise go test would replay a cached pass and hide the flakiness.

Debugging inside the container: --shell

When the run finishes, --shell opens a shell where the failing step ran: same directory, environment, toolchains and services. It prints the command that re-runs the step:

▶ Shell       inside the container at step 5 (Run ./.ci.govet.sh); type exit to finish
              re-run the step with: bash -e /home/runner/work/_temp/failtrace/step-5.sh

If an earlier step diverged, the shell opens at that step instead. The container is removed when you exit, unless you pass --keep.

Sharing the result: --report FILE

--report repro.md writes a Markdown report to paste into an issue or pull request. It includes the verdict, a CI-vs-local table, environment, differences, every step's result, and the output of the failing step from both sides. --report - prints it instead of the terminal summary. See docs/example-report.md, generated from the stretchr/testify run above with --runs 3.

Testing a fix: --source DIR

--source . swaps the commit CI tested for your local working tree, so you can check a fix on the same CI step before pushing it. FailTrace copies the tree's HEAD plus your uncommitted and untracked files into the workspace as one extra commit, so the checkout is clean the way it is in CI. Files your .gitignore excludes, such as .env or node_modules, are left out. Your working tree is only read. Setup steps, toolchains and services stay as CI had them.

From the testify run above, after fixing the two go vet errors without committing:

$ failtrace repro --source . https://github.com/stretchr/testify/actions/runs/39247781971
▶ Workspace   stretchr/testify from ~/src/testify (9272105, plus 1 changed file(s))
...
✓ Passes: the step that failed in CI passes with your working tree

Exit status

repro's exit status matches the failing step, so scripts and coding agents can loop on it without parsing the output:

Exit Verdict
0 not-reproduced: the step passed locally (with --source: your fix works)
2 reproduced
3 different-failure
4 diverged
5 flaky
1 FailTrace itself failed: bad arguments, Docker unavailable, a blocked plan

For details, --json prints the plan and the result: verdict, reasons, the CI and local failures, and every step's outcome.

failtrace repro --source . --json <run-url> 2>/dev/null | jq '.result | {verdict, reasons}'

Safety. repro runs the repository's code, including code from a pull request, inside a container on your machine. The container sees only the workspace, has no access to your home directory or the Docker socket, and gets no secrets unless you pass them with --secret NAME. The value is read from your environment, so it never appears in your shell history or the process list. Only reproduce runs whose code you're comfortable executing.

Limitations. These are reported instead of silently ignored:

  • A failing step that is an action rather than a script can't be replayed (verdict blocked).
  • Windows and macOS jobs are only approximated in Linux.
  • Steps run as root, where CI uses the runner user.
  • The runner image's many preinstalled tools aren't all present.
  • linux/amd64 jobs are emulated on ARM machines.
  • Artifacts from other jobs aren't available.

Roadmap

  • inspect: diagnose a failed run from its URL
  • plan: turn the failed job into a local reproduction plan: base image, exact commit, toolchain versions, env, steps to replay
  • repro: run the plan in Docker and compare the result with CI
  • Reports: --report writes a Markdown report with the verdict and the differences from CI
  • Flaky detection: --runs N repeats the failing step and reports flaky
  • --shell: drop into the container at the failing step
  • --source: test a local fix against the failing step before pushing
  • Exit codes per verdict, for scripts and coding agents
  • Releases: prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows, and a checksum-verifying install script
  • Homebrew and gh extension: brew install and gh failtrace <run-url>
  • Replaying common actions: translate actions such as golangci-lint-action into the commands they run, so failures in them can be reproduced too

Development

go test ./...                                     # unit tests (no network or Docker needed)
go test -race ./...
go vet ./...
go test -tags integration ./internal/repro/       # runs real containers; needs Docker
goreleaser release --snapshot --clean             # build release archives locally, publish nothing

CI runs all of the above on every pull request. To publish a release, push a version tag (git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0); release.yml builds and uploads the binaries.

Project layout:

cmd/failtrace/      CLI entry point
internal/cli/       commands and flags
internal/runurl/    run URL parsing and validation
internal/github/    minimal GitHub REST client and token lookup
internal/joblog/    job log parsing, failure extraction and classification
internal/workflow/  workflow YAML parsing, job/step/matrix matching
internal/inspect/   puts it all together into a report
internal/plan/      builds reproduction plans (image, commit, toolchains, env, steps)
internal/toolchain/ resolves toolchains to the builds setup-* actions use
internal/docker/    runs containers through the docker CLI
internal/repro/     executes a plan and compares the result with CI
internal/report/    terminal rendering

Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. The most useful contributions right now:

  • Failed runs that FailTrace gets wrong. Open an issue with the run URL and what you expected.
  • New failure signatures: test runners, package managers and compilers that aren't detected yet. These live in internal/joblog/analyze.go and need a test case.
  • More known actions: setup actions (internal/plan/toolchains.go) and actions that are safe to skip locally (internal/plan/actions.go). Each one is a single table entry.

[step 2] actions/download-artifact@9000827 downloads artifacts produced by another job or run; files it provides will be missing locally i [step 1] CI tested the merge of PR head 58b8dae into base 50234b4 (merge commit c484767), not the PR branch alone; the plan checks out that merge commit How the plan is built: The log is the source of truth for what ran. Scripts, shells and environment come from the step headers GitHub prints, so ${{ matrix.* }} and other expressions are already filled in. Composite actions show their inner steps. The exact commit CI tested. For pull requests that's a merge commit GitHub created, not your branch head. This is a common reason a failure "doesn't happen locally". The exact toolchain versions. "3.11" in the workflow becomes 3.11.18, read from the runner's tool cache paths. When the log doesn't show a version, it reads version files such as go.mod (including toolchain), .nvmrc, .python-version, .tool-versions and packageManager in package.json. The right base image. A job container: is used as is. Otherwise it picks the Ubuntu version matching the runner image the job actually got. What to skip and what to flag. Caches, uploads and coverage reporters are skipped. Downloaded artifacts, service containers, secrets, unknown actions, and tools used without a setup step (they were preinstalled on the runner) are reported as issues. The verdict is ready (nothing known to be missing), partial (it can run, but some parts are approximated or missing) or blocked (the failing step is an action, not a script, so it can't be replayed yet). Reproducing a failure failtrace repro builds the plan and runs it in Docker, then compares the result with CI's failure. failtrace repro <run-url> failtrace repro --keep <run-url> # keep the container to poke around afterwards API_TOKEN=... failtrace repro --secret API_TOKEN <run-url> failtrace repro --toolchain node=20.11.1 <run-url> # fill in or override a toolchain failtrace repro --platform linux/arm64 <run-url> # run natively on Apple silicon (faster, less exact) failtrace repro --runs 10 <run-url> # is it flaky? failtrace repro --shell <run-url> # debug inside the container afterwards failtrace repro --report repro.md <run-url> # Markdown report for an issue or PR You need Docker (Docker Desktop, colima, OrbStack, …) and git. Real output for a failed stretchr/testify run, where go vet failed under Go oldstable. FailTrace resolved oldstable to the exact Go 1.26.9 build CI used, checked out the PR merge commit CI tested, and replayed the steps: $ failtrace repro --platform linux/arm64 https://github.com/stretchr/testify/actions/runs/39247781971 Reproducing stretchr/testify · build (oldstable) · plan ready ▶ Image failtrace-env:08414601e6c4aef4 (cached) ▶ Workspace stretchr/testify @ 9272105 ▶ [3/5] Run ./.ci.gogenerate.sh ✓ exit code 0 (17.7s) ▶ [4/5] Run ./.ci.gofmt.sh ✓ exit code 0 (7.4s) ▶ [5/5] Run ./.ci.govet.sh ← failed in CI │ assert/assertion_compare_test.go:85:13: non-constant format string in call to (*testing.common).Errorf │ assert/assertion_compare_test.go:94:13: non-constant format string in call to (*testing.common).Errorf ✗ exit code 1 (10.7s) ✓ Reproduced: the step fails locally the same way it failed in CI • the same error: assert/assertion_compare_test.go:<n>:<n>: non-constant format string in call to (*testing.common).Errorf CI Local Exit code 1 1 Failure lint / format check lint / format check Steps 4 passed · 1 failed (39s total) Image failtrace-env:08414601e6c4aef4 linux/arm64 Differences from CI - the image is plain ubuntu:24.04 with common runner packages; GitHub's runner image has far more preinstalled - steps run as root; on GitHub's runners they run as the `runner` user with passwordless sudo - running linux/arm64, but CI ran linux/amd64 Without --platform, the job runs as linux/amd64 like CI did. On an Apple silicon Mac that means emulation: the same reproduction took about 9 minutes instead of 40 seconds, with the same verdict. What happens: Environment image. The plan's base image, plus the packages every GitHub Ubuntu runner has (git, curl, build tools, python3, jq, sudo, …), plus the toolchains. Go, Node and Python are the same builds setup-go, setup-node and setup-python download, installed under /opt/hostedtoolcache where CI keeps them. uv, pnpm and Rust are installed from their releases. The image is tagged by a hash of its contents, so it's only built once per environment. Workspace. The exact commit CI tested is fetched on your machine the way actions/checkout does it, with the same fetch depth, and mounted at the same path as on the runner (/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>, or /__w/... for container jobs). If GitHub has since replaced a pull request's merge commit, the merge is recreated locally. Services. Service containers start in the job container's network namespace, so localhost:5432 and postgres:5432 both work, and FailTrace waits for their health checks. Steps. Run steps replay in order with the shell, environment and working directory CI used. $GITHUB_ENV and $GITHUB_PATH carry over between steps. The failing step's output streams live. Verdict. reproduced: the same tests failed, or the same error or exit code. different-failure not-reproduced: the step passed locally. diverged: an earlier step failed locally, so the failing step never ran. flaky: with --runs, the step failed in some runs but not all. A list of known differences from CI comes with every verdict. Flaky failures: --runs N The setup steps run once, then the failing step runs N times in the same container, so repeats are cheap. If it fails only some of the time, the verdict is flaky ("the step failed in 3 of 10 runs"). Go's test cache is bypassed for these runs (GOFLAGS=-count=1). Otherwise go test would replay a cached pass and hide the flakiness. Debugging inside the container: --shell When the run finishes, --shell opens a shell where the failing step ran: same directory, environment, toolchains and services. It prints the command that re-runs the step: ▶ Shell inside the container at step 5 (Run ./.ci.govet.sh); type exit to finish re-run the step with: bash -e /home/runner/work/_temp/failtrace/step-5.sh If an earlier step diverged, the shell opens at that step instead. The container is removed when you exit, unless you pass --keep. Sharing the result: --report FILE --report repro.md writes a Markdown report to paste into an issue or pull request. It includes the verdict, a CI-vs-local table, environment, differences, every step's result, and the output of the failing step from both sides. --report - prints it instead of the terminal summary. See docs/example-report.md, generated from the stretchr/testify run above with --runs 3. Testing a fix: --source DIR --source . swaps the commit CI tested for your local working tree, so you can check a fix on the same CI step before pushing it. FailTrace copies the tree's HEAD plus your uncommitted and untracked files into the workspace as one extra commit, so the checkout is clean the way it is in CI. Files your .gitignore excludes, such as .env or node_modules, are left out. Your working tree is only read. Setup steps, toolchains and services stay as CI had them. From the testify run above, after fixing the two go vet errors without committing: $ failtrace repro --source . https://github.com/stretchr/testify/actions/runs/39247781971 ▶ Workspace stretchr/testify from ~/src/testify (9272105, plus 1 changed file(s)) ... ✓ Passes: the step that failed in CI passes with your working tree Exit status repro's exit status matches the failing step, so scripts and coding agents can loop on it without parsing the output: Exit Verdict 0 not-reproduced: the step passed locally (with --source: your fix works) 2 reproduced 3 different-failure 4 diverged 5 flaky 1 FailTrace itself failed: bad arguments, Docker unavailable, a blocked plan For details, --json prints the plan and the result: verdict, reasons, the CI and local failures, and every step's outcome. failtrace repro --source . --json <run-url> 2>/dev/null | jq '.result | {verdict, reasons}' Safety. repro runs the repository's code, including code from a pull request, inside a container on your machine. The container sees only the workspace, has no access to your home directory or the Docker socket, and gets no secrets unless you pass them with --secret NAME. The value is read from your environment, so it never appears in your shell history or the process list. Only reproduce runs whose code you're comfortable executing. Limitations. These are reported instead of silently ignored: A failing step that is an action rather than a script can't be replayed (verdict blocked). Windows and macOS jobs are only approximated in Linux. Steps run as root, where CI uses the runner user. The runner image's many preinstalled tools aren't all present. linux/amd64 jobs are emulated on ARM machines. Artifacts from other jobs aren't available. Roadmap inspect: diagnose a failed run from its URL plan: turn the failed job into a local reproduction plan: base image, exact commit, toolchain versions, env, steps to replay repro: run the plan in Docker and compare the result with CI Reports: --report writes a Markdown report with the verdict and the differences from CI Flaky detection: --runs N repeats the failing step and reports flaky --shell: drop into the container at the failing step --source: test a local fix against the failing step before pushing Exit codes per verdict, for scripts and coding agents Releases: prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows, and a checksum-verifying install script Homebrew and gh extension: brew install and gh failtrace <run-url> Replaying common actions: translate actions such as golangci-lint-action into the commands they run, so failures in them can be reproduced too Development go test ./... # unit tests (no network or Docker needed) go test -race ./... go vet ./... go test -tags integration ./internal/repro/ # runs real containers; needs Docker goreleaser release --snapshot --clean # build release archives locally, publish nothing CI runs all of the above on every pull request. To publish a release, push a version tag (git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0); release.yml builds and uploads the binaries. The most useful contributions right now: Failed runs that FailTrace gets wrong. Open an issue with the run URL and what you expected. New failure signatures: test runners, package managers and compilers that aren't detected yet. These live in internal/joblog/analyze.go and need a test case. More known actions: setup actions (internal/plan/toolchains.go) and actions that are safe to skip locally (internal/plan/actions.go). Each one is a single table entry. License MIT

content_html_zh:
Stop guessing why CI failed. Reproduce it locally.

Paste a failed GitHub Actions run URL. FailTrace finds the job and step that failed, matches them to the workflow file at that exact commit, pulls the failure out of the logs, and tells you what stands between you and reproducing it on your machine.

failtrace inspect https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789   # why did it fail?
failtrace plan    https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789   # how would it be reproduced?
failtrace repro   https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789   # reproduce it in Docker
Status: early development. All three commands work. repro covers Linux jobs whose failing step is a run: script. See the roadmap and limitations.

Why not act?

act runs your workflows locally, and it's great at that. FailTrace answers a different question: why did this particular run fail, and can I make it fail the same way here?

  • It starts from a failed run, not a workflow file. You get the exact commit, attempt, job, matrix combination, and failing step. 没有什么可配置的。
  • It focuses on the failure. The goal is to replay only what the failing step needs, not the whole workflow.
  • It gives you a verdict. You get a diagnosis now. Later you'll also get reproduced / not reproduced / flaky, plus what differed between CI and your machine.

例子

Real output for a failed prometheus/prometheus run (trimmed):

✗ CI · prometheus/prometheus
  "remote/otlp: remove delta-to-cumulative conversion"
  pull_request · on codex/remove-otlp-deltatocumulative · @ cf7d324 · attempt 1 · failure

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
✗ Job: Go tests  (failure)
  Runner     ubuntu-latest → ubuntu-26.04 (20261116.202.1) · runner 2.338.2
  Workflow   .github/workflows/ci.yml → jobs.test_go

  Steps
    ✓  5  Run make GO_ONLY=1 SKIP_GOLANGCI_LINT=1
    ✓  6  Run go test ./tsdb/ -test.tsdb-isolation=false
    ✗  7  Run make -C documentation/examples/remote_storage  ← failed here
    ○  8  Run make -C documentation/examples (skipped)

  Failed step  #7 Run make -C documentation/examples/remote_storage
    shell: sh -e {0}
    $ make -C documentation/examples/remote_storage

  Diagnosis  files out of date (a check produced a git diff) · exit code 2

  Log excerpt (10 lines around the first error in "Run make -C documentation/examples/remote_storage")
    │ >> running check for unused/missing packages in go.mod
    │ go mod tidy
    │ go: downloading github.com/oapi-codegen/nullable v1.1.0
    │ diff --git a/documentation/examples/remote_storage/go.mod b/documentation/examples/remote_storage/go.mod
    │ --- a/documentation/examples/remote_storage/go.mod
    │ +++ b/documentation/examples/remote_storage/go.mod

  Reproduction notes
    ! job runs inside container quay.io/prometheus/golang-builder:1.27-base

The log ends with hundreds of lines of go.sum diff. FailTrace centres the excerpt on the first error line so you see the cause, go mod tidy changing go.mod, instead of the noise after it.

安装

macOS and Linux, using the install script. It downloads the latest release for your platform and verifies its SHA-256 checksum:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ri4dH/failtrace/main/scripts/install.sh | sh

It installs to /usr/local/bin if that's writable, otherwise to ~/.local/bin. Set FAILTRACE_INSTALL_DIR to choose, or FAILTRACE_VERSION=v0.1.0 to pin a release.

Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows (amd64 and arm64) are on the releases page, with a checksums.txt.

With Go 1.24+:

go install github.com/Ri4dH/failtrace/cmd/failtrace@latest

来自来源：

git clone https://github.com/Ri4dH/failtrace
cd failtrace
go build -o bin/failtrace ./cmd/failtrace

Usage

# All failed jobs in the latest attempt of a run
failtrace inspect https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789

# A single job (the URL you get from clicking a job in the Actions UI)
failtrace inspect https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789/job/987654321

# A specific attempt of a re-run workflow
failtrace inspect https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789/attempts/2

# Show more log context, or emit JSON for scripts and other tools
failtrace inspect -n 60 <run-url>
failtrace inspect --json <run-url> | jq '.failed_jobs[0].failure'

# A compact summary to paste into a coding assistant
failtrace inspect --llm <run-url> | pbcopy
Flag 默认 描述
--json off Print the report as JSON
--llm off Print a compact plain-text summary for a language model's prompt
-n, --lines 25 Log lines to show from the failed step
--job all failed Inspect only this job ID

Colour output turns off automatically when stdout is not a terminal, or when NO_COLOR is set.

For coding assistants: --llm

--llm prints only what a model needs to fix the failure: the failing step, its command and relevant env, the exit code, errors, failing tests, and the log from the first error. It leaves out step lists, runner metadata, the variables setup actions export, and go test -v progress lines and progress bars. Error lines appear once, and matrix jobs that failed the same way collapse into one line.

Measured on real failed runs, compared with the raw logs of their failed jobs:

Run Raw logs --llm
stretchr/testify (go vet + Go version) 38 KB 1.2 KB
pytest-dev/pytest (pytest failure) 125 KB 3.7 KB
vitejs/vite (two Vitest failures) 306 KB 3.9 KB
prometheus/prometheus (Go test failure) 8.3 MB 1.8 KB

验证

FailTrace needs a GitHub token, even for public repositories, because the logs API requires one. It looks in this order:

  1. GITHUB_TOKEN
  2. GH_TOKEN
  3. gh auth token (if you use the GitHub CLI, this already works)

Private repositories need a token that can read Actions on that repo. GitHub Enterprise Server URLs work too: the API base becomes https://<host>/api/v3.

What inspect reports

  • Run context: workflow, event, branch, commit, attempt.
  • Job → workflow mapping: finds the job definition, including jobs named like test (ubuntu-latest, 1.22) or Lint ${{ matrix.tool }}, and recovers the matrix values.
  • Runner: the requested label and the actual runner image and version, from the log.
  • Failed step: its definition (run, uses, with, env, shell, working directory). The command shown is the one printed in the log, with expressions already filled in.
  • Diagnosis: exit code, error annotations, failing test names (Go, pytest, Jest, Vitest, Cargo, RSpec), and a category: Category Example signal test --- FAIL: TestX, FAILED tests/x.py::test_y build error TS2304, undefined: foo, error[E0425] dependency npm ERR! code ERESOLVE, missing go.sum entry lint golangci-lint, eslint, ruff steps generated-diff a check that printed diff --git (tidy, codegen, formatters) timeout exceeded the maximum execution time out-of-memory exit code 137, heap out of memory
  • Reproduction notes: anything that makes a local repro harder. That means service containers, job containers, secrets the step uses, reusable workflows, and macOS or Windows runners.

It also explains edge cases instead of failing silently: runs that failed before any job started, dynamic workflows with no file in the repo, and logs that have expired.

Planning a reproduction

failtrace plan works out how to reproduce the failed job locally and prints the plan. It doesn't run anything yet.

failtrace plan https://github.com/owner/repo/actions/runs/123456789
failtrace plan --job 987654321 <run-url>     # pick a job when several failed
failtrace plan --json <run-url>              # the full plan, including every env var

How the plan is built:

  • The log is the source of truth for what ran. Scripts, shells and environment come from the step headers GitHub prints, so ${{ matrix.* }} and other expressions are already filled in. Composite actions show their inner steps.
  • The exact commit CI tested. For pull requests that's a merge commit GitHub created, not your branch head. This is a common reason a failure "doesn't happen locally".
  • The exact toolchain versions. "3.11" in the workflow becomes 3.11.18, read from the runner's tool cache paths. When the log doesn't show a version, it reads version files such as go.mod (including toolchain), .nvmrc, .python-version, .tool-versions and packageManager in package.json.
  • The right base image. A job container: is used as is. Otherwise it picks the Ubuntu version matching the runner image the job actually got.
  • What to skip and what to flag. Caches, uploads and coverage reporters are skipped. Downloaded artifacts, service containers, secrets, unknown actions, and tools used without a setup step (they were preinstalled on the runner) are reported as issues.

The verdict is ready (nothing known to be missing), partial (it can run, but some parts are approximated or missing) or blocked (the failing step is an action, not a script, so it can't be replayed yet).

Supported setup actions: actions/setup-go, setup-node, setup-python, setup-java, setup-dotnet, ruby/setup-ruby, dtolnay/rust-toolchain, actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain, pnpm/action-setup, pnpm/setup, astral-sh/setup-uv, oven-sh/setup-bun and denoland/setup-deno.

Reproducing a failure

failtrace repro builds the plan and runs it in Docker, then compares the result with CI's failure.

failtrace repro <run-url>
failtrace repro --keep <run-url>                     # keep the container to poke around afterwards
API_TOKEN=... failtrace repro --secret API_TOKEN <run-url>
failtrace repro --toolchain node=20.11.1 <run-url>   # fill in or override a toolchain
failtrace repro --platform linux/arm64 <run-url>     # run natively on Apple silicon (faster, less exact)
failtrace repro --runs 10 <run-url>                  # is it flaky?
failtrace repro --shell <run-url>                    # debug inside the container afterwards
failtrace repro --report repro.md <run-url>          # Markdown report for an issue or PR

You need Docker (Docker Desktop, colima, OrbStack, …) and git.

What happens:

  1. Environment image. The plan's base image, plus the packages every GitHub Ubuntu runner has (git, curl, build tools, python3, jq, sudo, …), plus the toolchains. Go, Node and Python are the same builds setup-go, setup-node and setup-python download, installed under /opt/hostedtoolcache where CI keeps them. uv, pnpm and Rust are installed from their releases. The image is tagged by a hash of its contents, so it's only built once per environment.
  2. Workspace. The exact commit CI tested is fetched on your machine the way actions/checkout does it, with the same fetch depth, and mounted at the same path as on the runner (/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>, or /__w/... for container jobs). If GitHub has since replaced a pull request's merge commit, the merge is recreated locally.
  3. Services. Service containers start in the job container's network namespace, so localhost:5432 and postgres:5432 both work, and FailTrace waits for their health checks.
  4. Steps. Run steps replay in order with the shell, environment and working directory CI used. $GITHUB_ENV and $GITHUB_PATH carry over between steps. The failing step's output streams live.
  5. Verdict. reproduced: the same tests failed, or the same error or exit code. different-failure not-reproduced: the step passed locally. diverged: an earlier step failed locally, so the failing step never ran. flaky: with --runs, the step failed in some runs but not all. A list of known differences from CI comes with every verdict.

Flaky failures: --runs N

The setup steps run once, then the failing step runs N times in the same container, so repeats are cheap. If it fails only some of the time, the verdict is flaky ("the step failed in 3 of 10 runs"). Go's test cache is bypassed for these runs (GOFLAGS=-count=1). Otherwise go test would replay a cached pass and hide the flakiness.

Debugging inside the container: --shell

When the run finishes, --shell opens a shell where the failing step ran: same directory, environment, toolchains and services. It prints the command that re-runs the step:

▶ Shell       inside the container at step 5 (Run ./.ci.govet.sh); type exit to finish
              re-run the step with: bash -e /home/runner/work/_temp/failtrace/step-5.sh

If an earlier step diverged, the shell opens at that step instead. The container is removed when you exit, unless you pass --keep.

Sharing the result: --report FILE

--report repro.md writes a Markdown report to paste into an issue or pull request. It includes the verdict, a CI-vs-local table, environment, differences, every step's result, and the output of the failing step from both sides. --report - prints it instead of the terminal summary. See docs/example-report.md, generated from the stretchr/testify run above with --runs 3.

Testing a fix: --source DIR

--source . swaps the commit CI tested for your local working tree, so you can check a fix on the same CI step before pushing it. FailTrace copies the tree's HEAD plus your uncommitted and untracked files into the workspace as one extra commit, so the checkout is clean the way it is in CI. Files your .gitignore excludes, such as .env or node_modules, are left out. Your working tree is only read. Setup steps, toolchains and services stay as CI had them.

✓ Passes: the step that failed in CI passes with your working tree

Exit status

repro's exit status matches the failing step, so scripts and coding agents can loop on it without parsing the output:

Exit 判决
0 not-reproduced: the step passed locally (with --source: your fix works)
2 reproduced
3 different-failure
4 diverged
5 flaky
1 FailTrace itself failed: bad arguments, Docker unavailable, a blocked plan

For details, --json prints the plan and the result: verdict, reasons, the CI and local failures, and every step's outcome.

failtrace repro --source . --json <run-url> 2>/dev/null | jq '.result | {verdict, reasons}'

安全。 repro runs the repository's code, including code from a pull request, inside a container on your machine. The container sees only the workspace, has no access to your home directory or the Docker socket, and gets no secrets unless you pass them with --secret NAME. The value is read from your environment, so it never appears in your shell history or the process list. Only reproduce runs whose code you're comfortable executing.

Limitations. These are reported instead of silently ignored:

  • A failing step that is an action rather than a script can't be replayed (verdict blocked).
  • Windows and macOS jobs are only approximated in Linux.
  • Steps run as root, where CI uses the runner user.
  • The runner image's many preinstalled tools aren't all present.
  • linux/amd64 jobs are emulated on ARM machines.
  • Artifacts from other jobs aren't available.

路线图

  • inspect: diagnose a failed run from its URL
  • plan: turn the failed job into a local reproduction plan: base image, exact commit, toolchain versions, env, steps to replay
  • repro: run the plan in Docker and compare the result with CI
  • Reports: --report writes a Markdown report with the verdict and the differences from CI
  • Flaky detection: --runs N repeats the failing step and reports flaky
  • --shell: drop into the container at the failing step
  • --source: test a local fix against the failing step before pushing
  • Exit codes per verdict, for scripts and coding agents
  • Releases: prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows, and a checksum-verifying install script
  • Homebrew and gh extension: brew install and gh failtrace <run-url>
  • Replaying common actions: translate actions such as golangci-lint-action into the commands they run, so failures in them can be reproduced too

发展

go test ./...                                     # unit tests (no network or Docker needed)
go test -race ./...
go vet ./...
go test -tags integration ./internal/repro/       # runs real containers; needs Docker
goreleaser release --snapshot --clean             # build release archives locally, publish nothing

CI runs all of the above on every pull request. To publish a release, push a version tag (git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0); release.yml builds and uploads the binaries.
